svg.title: Formal Levi normalization and the moving-point Hecke covector
svg.desc: For a nonnilpotent Lie value, its compatible Jordan components determine a reductive centralizer and an integral cocharacter with nonzero pairing. An invertible off-Levi adjoint operator removes higher coefficients over every coefficient ring. The arc quotient retains automorphisms, its cotangent is an annihilator, and crystal minus coordinate transport gives the positive logarithmic derivative. In the exact SL3 trace-form example the residue is six dx.
svg.text: A nonnilpotent value gives a nonzero curve covector
Algebraically closed characteristic zero • arbitrary connected reductive G
1. Compatible Jordan components and their centralizer
C = H + N, [H,N] = 0; H semisimple, Nʳ = 0 in a faithful V
H ≠ 0 ⇒ M = C_G(H) = C_G(S) = C_G(λ)
α(λ) = 0 ⇔ α(H) = 0; λ is central in M
B(dλ,N) = 0; B(C,dλ) = B(H,dλ) ≠ 0
The finite root hyperplanes and the pairing hyperplane are avoided together.
HC.1–HC.8 • central torus directions are retained
2. Formal normalization over every coefficient algebra R
g = m ⊕ n, A₀ ∈ m(R), ad(A₀)|n_R invertible
Degree n: Xₙ = (ad(A₀)|n_R)⁻¹Yₙ, hₙ = exp(uⁿXₙ)
Off-Levi coefficient: Yₙ + [Xₙ,A₀] = 0
h = lim hₙ···h₁, h(0) = 1, Ad_h A(u) ∈ m(R[[u]])
Two identity-branch normalizations differ by a left M(R[[u]]) frame.
HC.9–HC.12 • a determinant-open condition, including nonreduced R
3. Local Hecke groupoid and the moving point
α: P₂|D× → P₁|D×; loop g, frame change a g b⁻¹
Tangent [ g[[u]]² → g((u)) ]: (a,b) ↦ Ad_g⁻¹ a − b
Degrees −1,0 retain stabilizers; η annihilates both arc directions.
η₂ = α*η₁, both ηᵢ regular; u = t − x
Crystal − coordinate: g(u+ε) − g(u) ↦ g⁻¹g′
g = u^λ ⇒ ξₓ = Res⟨η,g⁻¹g′⟩ dx = ⟨A₀,dλ⟩ dx
HC.15–HC.22 • the positive sign and base differential are essential
4. Exact SL₃ example, with B(A,D) = tr(AD)
C = diag(1,1,−2) + E₁₂; λ(u) = diag(u,u,u⁻²)
A(u) = C + uE₂₃; X₁ = E₂₃/3 − E₁₃/9; h = I + uX₁
[C,X₁] = E₂₃, X₁² = 0; h A(u) h⁻¹ = C exactly
HC.13–HC.14; solved Exercise 3.P • nilpotent block E₁₂ has zero diagonal trace
Formal local calculations; the global Hecke image and regularity remain to be proved.
